newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to increase T-bill volumes, maturities.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to increase T-bill volumes, maturities.

text.p: Ukraine plans to issue 3.5 billion hryvnias nominal of Treasury bills this year, up from a previously planned 2.5 billion hryvnias, and issue new paper in maturities of up to three years, the deputy finance minister said on Tuesday.

"The government resolution foresees increasing the volume to 3.5 billion hryvnia in 1997 from 2.5 billion hryvnia, and also foreseen is the possibility of establishing maturities of one and a half, two, and three years," Valery Lytvyn told Reuters.
He said the government signed the resolution on March 5 but had not yet established when the changes would take place.

"I wouldn't say this would happen in one, two, or six days, since we have to take a good look at the market, but we're interested in starting the release of new maturities in as short a time as possible," Lytvyn said.
In 1996 Ukraine issued about 3.3 billion hryvnias of T-bills.
At the most recent auction last week, yields on three-, six-, nine and 12-month paper were between 25 and 38 percent. T-bills are usually issued twice weekly by the Finance Ministry.

Foreign investors attracted by slower inflation and relatively high yields have become major buyers of the bills. But in recent weeks the Finance Ministry has started limiting issues of short-term paper to boost buying of longer-term bills.
The government has been planning to raise three billion hryvnias from discount T-bills this year to finance the deficit, compared to 1.5 billion hryvnias in 1996.
Total volumes will be firmly established once the parliament approves this month or next the overdue 1997 budget.
Inflation has been forecast at 24-25 percent in 1997, compared to 39.7 percent in 1996.
